newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan recovery firming despite sales tax rise--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan recovery firming despite sales tax rise--BOJ.

text.p: The Japanese economic recovery is getting firmer despite effects from a rise in the sales tax, and the recovery is likely to continue, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.
Matsushita said the negative effects of the tax rise were being felt most strongly at present, but added that the economy's gradual recovery trend was intact.
"Under such conditions, the firmness of the recovery in the economy is continuing to increase," he said.

He said production and capital spending were still on a rising trend despite a fall in public spending and housing investment. Matsushita added that although private consumption fell after the introduction of the rise in the sales tax in April, it was likely that the trend of an increase in consumption would resume.
The trend was likely to resume and continue, taking into account the recent pickup in consumption, he said.
"The economy may experience a temporary slowdown for the time being, but looking at this mechanism, the likelihood is strong that the economic recovery will continue in the future," Matsushita said.
But he said the central bank needs to monitor future movements in private consumption and corporate activity.
"For the time being we will continue to carry out monetary policy putting emphasis on strengthening the basis of the economic recovery."
On prices, Matsushita said both consumer and wholesale prices rose in April due to the sales tax increase, but said that disregarding the effect of the tax rise, prices remained stable.
Matsushita said there was no change in the central bank's assessment that prices had clearly stopped falling.
"Prices have been stable due to stability in crude oil prices and the correction of the yen's weakness. But we will continue to watch future developments," Matsushita said.
